messages.text: hi, time for yearly hike, where and when? thoughts?

Great, love that it's that time again! My vote is for something with real elevation gain and technical terrain — somewhere like the North Cascades or the Wind River Range would give us a proper challenge and stunning scenery that actually rewards the effort. Late July or August tends to be the sweet spot for high-country routes when snow has cleared but crowds haven't peaked. What's the group's general fitness level looking like this year?

Both options sound amazing, but before I get too excited I'd love to know what we're looking at cost-wise — travel to the North Cascades versus the Wind River Range could be pretty different depending on where everyone is flying from. Can we nail down rough estimates for flights, permits, and gear rentals before we commit to either? I'm also wondering if there are any less expensive alternatives that still check the scenery and challenge boxes.
how about archies ? I hear its great in September?

Arches is a really interesting suggestion — it's generally more accessible than the other options, with well-maintained trails and paved paths to many of the iconic features, which I appreciate. That said, September in Arches can still be quite hot, so I'd want to understand how that affects trail conditions and whether everyone in the group can manage heat comfortably. It also tends to be less technically demanding than the North Cascades or Wind River Range, so worth checking if that works for what Alex is looking for too.
